watch_outs: Missing bank account: CBP pays refunds only electronically; without confirmed details your $145,551 could join the $1.1B already on hold.
Surety‑paid entries: No CAPE process exists; filing them now guarantees rejection. Wait for CBP guidance.
Open protests: CAPE rejects protested entries. Withdrawal is only allowed if the protest was IEEPA‑only and within 80 days of liquidation — otherwise the protest must stand.
Warehouse entry (type 21/22): Since July 7, 2026 CAPE rejects these; you must file withdrawal entries (types 31/32/34/38) instead. Entry Q7Z-4103424-9 ($1,640) is affected.

explanations.Q7Z-4103455-3: This entry is suspended under AD/CVD rules, so the $1,520 in IEEPA duties plus $88.11 interest can be removed now, but the actual refund won’t be paid until Commerce lifts the suspension. File the claim in ACE (CAPE) as soon as practical — there’s no statutory deadline shown, but earlier filing gets you in line sooner. The timing of the suspension lift is uncertain, so the refund date is unknown.
explanations.Q7Z-4103309-2: This entry requires a Post Summary Correction (PSC) to be filed and accepted before you can submit a CAPE claim for the IEEPA refund. You must file the PSC first; once CAPE accepts the entry, the PSC can no longer be filed, and the PSC itself does not claim the refund. There is no deadline or liquidation date provided, so the timing is uncertain—act promptly to avoid missing any future cutoff. The guidance carries a “P” (probable) confidence tag, meaning the requirement is likely but not guaranteed; confirm with your broker or CBP if anything is unclear.
explanations.Q7Z-4101559-4: This entry liquidated 81–180 days ago and you’re not a court plaintiff, so the CAPE refund path isn’t available right now. To keep any chance of recovery, you must file a protest in ACE before the 180‑day deadline on **2026‑10‑27** (two days from now) and/or discuss a Court of International Trade case with counsel. The principal at stake is $1,567.50 plus $125.01 interest. The rule’s “P” confidence tag means the protest/CIT route is plausible but not guaranteed—outcome depends on facts and legal arguments not yet tested.
explanations.K4M-9231751-6: This entry liquidated 81–180 days ago and you are not the importer of record, so any refund belongs to that party and there is no CAPE path available today. To preserve your rights you must file a protest in ACE before the 180‑day deadline on 2026‑11‑24 (30 days left) and/or consult counsel about a CIT case. The liquidation date (2026‑05‑28) is estimated from the entry date and the importer‑of‑record discrepancy means you should verify everything in ACE before acting.
explanations.Q7Z-4102801-9: This entry carries only a $530 Section 122 surcharge — no IEEPA duty — so it cannot be refunded through the CAPE process. To keep any legal rights alive, you (or your broker) must file a protest within 180 days of the entry’s liquidation. The liquidation date isn’t shown here, so the exact protest deadline is unknown until you confirm it with your broker or CBP. Ask your broker or counsel promptly whether a protest is warranted and when it must be filed.
explanations.Q7Z-4103107-0: Your entry has an open protest, and CAPE automatically rejects any protested entry — so the protest must be resolved before a CAPE refund can proceed. If the protest covers **only** the IEEPA tariffs and today is within 80 days of the 2026-06-25 liquidation, withdraw the protest and file the CAPE claim; otherwise, leave the protest in place. The critical unknowns are (1) whether the protest’s scope is limited to IEEPA and (2) whether you’re still inside that 80-day window — both need confirmation before you act.
explanations.Q7Z-4103424-9: Your warehouse entry (Q7Z-4103424-9) for $1,640 plus $69.31 interest can no longer be processed in CAPE because warehouse entries (types 21/22) have been rejected since July 7, 2026. You must file withdrawal entries (types 31, 32, 34, or 38) instead to pursue any refund. No deadline or liquidation date is shown in the data, so the timing is uncertain. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning it may still be proposed or subject to change.
explanations.Q7Z-4101104-9: This entry liquidated on August 9, 2026, so you have a CAPE refund of $1,810 principal plus $115.34 interest that CBP must accept if filed by day 80 — October 28, 2026 (three days from now). File the claim in CAPE immediately; the 80‑day window is a hard deadline. The “P” confidence tag means the rule interpretation is provisional, and the two listed programs (India Russian oil, Reciprocal Aug 2025 rate) may affect eligibility but aren’t quantified here.
